files.lesson.md: --- order: 3 unit: area node: AC9M7M01 n2 title: Area problems summary: "Pick the base and the height at a right angle to it, put both lengths in the same unit, and split a shape into rectangles and triangles. Area is in square units: m², cm²." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "How much paint for the end wall of a house, with its triangle of roof? Real shapes mix rectangles and triangles, and real measurements mix metres and centimetres." connection: gable-paint app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8275 url: http://127.0.0.1:8275/index.html readySelector: "#sl-s" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: area.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Base 10 cm, height 4 cm, and a slanted side of 5 cm. The area uses the base and the height at a right angle to it: $\\tfrac{1}{2} \\times 10 \\times 4 = 20$ cm²." } explainClip: query: { code: "@area.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Choose the right lengths" say: "Use the base and the height at a right angle." clip: - caption: { text: "Three lengths: base, height, and a slanted side.", say: "There are three lengths: a base, a height, and a slanted side." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "The slant changes as the top moves. The area does not.", say: "The slanted side changes as the top moves. The area does not." } - click: Move the top left - click: Move the top left - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "= 20" } - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "So use the base and the height: ½ × 10 × 4 = 20.", say: "So use the base and the height: twenty square centimetres." } - wait: 1200 --- Before you multiply anything, read what the question gives you. What shape is it, and are the lengths in the same unit? ## Predict: metres and centimetres ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to an area for a 4 m by 250 cm room shows whether they convert to one unit before multiplying." check: type: predict q: "A room is 4 m long and 250 cm wide. What is its area?" options: ["10 m²", "1000 m²", "1000 cm", "6.5 m²"] actual: "10 m². 250 cm = 2.5 m, and 4 × 2.5 = 10 m². 1000 mixes metres with centimetres; 6.5 adds." ``` Write both lengths in metres first. ## Run: a 4 m by 2.5 m room ```step stage: run insight: "Building the room in metres on the board shows the area in m², with a half-metre row of squares." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#run", height: 520 } check: { type: board, text: "Make a rectangle with base 4 m and height 2.5 m (250 cm). What is its area? Was your prediction right?", when: "b = 4 and h = 2.5", explain: "4 × 2.5 = 10 m²: two full rows of 4 square metres, and a half row of 4 halves." } ``` Each grid square is 1 m by 1 m: one square metre. That's three moves to sort an area problem out: - **Choose the base and its height.** The height is at a right angle to the base; a slanted side is not needed. - **Use one unit.** Change every length to the same unit (100 cm = 1 m) before you multiply. Area comes out in square units: m² or cm². - **Split the shape.** A shape made of rectangles and triangles has area equal to the sum of the parts (or a big shape minus a missing part). ## Investigate: choose, convert, split ```step stage: investigate insight: "Area problems need the right lengths, one unit and a split into parts; Ivy multiplies centimetres by metres. Students own the working for the house shape and pick the reason at the key step." tasks: - check: type: reasoning q: "The end wall of a house is a rectangle 6 m wide and 4 m high, with a triangle of roof on top: base 6 m, height 3 m. Find the area of the whole wall. Write your steps." steps: - ["Rectangle: $6 \\times 4 = 24$ m²", "a rectangle's area is length × width"] - ["Triangle: $\\tfrac{1}{2} \\times 6 \\times 3 = 9$ m²", "a triangle is half of base × height"] - ["Wall: $24 + 9 = 33$ m²", "the whole is the sum of its parts"] picks: - step: 2 options: ["A triangle is half of base × height", "A triangle is base × height", "Add the base and the height"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is the parallelogram two triangles make: 18, not 9.", "Area multiplies lengths."] answer: "33" feedback: - ["42", "The roof triangle is half of 6 × 3: 9, not 18."] - ["24", "That is the rectangle only. Add the roof."] explain: "24 + 9 = 33 m²." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ivy" text: "Ivy finds the area of a rug. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: area-units explain: "Line 3: 50 is in centimetres and 2 in metres. Change 50 cm to 0.5 m: 0.5 × 2 = 1 m²." - picture: { ref: area.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A triangle with base 10 cm, height 4 cm and a slanted side of 5 cm." } check: type: question q: "Which two lengths give this triangle's area?" options: ["The base 10 cm and the height 4 cm", "The base 10 cm and the slanted side 5 cm", "The height 4 cm and the slanted side 5 cm", "All three: 10 + 4 + 5"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The slanted side is not at a right angle to the base.", "Use the base and its height.", "Adding the sides gives a perimeter, not an area."] explain: "½ × 10 × 4 = 20 cm². The 5 cm side is extra information." ``` ### Three moves Here are the three moves. ```worked \tfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 4 = 20 \text{ cm}^2 :: Choose: the base and the height at a right angle to it. Ignore the slanted 5 cm side. 250 \text{ cm} = 2.5 \text{ m}, \quad 4 \times 2.5 = 10 \text{ m}^2 :: Convert: both lengths in metres, then multiply. 24 + 9 = 33 \text{ m}^2 :: Split: a rectangle (6 × 4) plus a triangle (½ × 6 × 3). 8 \times 5 - 3 \times 2 = 34 \text{ m}^2 :: Or subtract: a rectangle with a corner missing is the big rectangle minus the corner. ``` Your working can be short notes. Then choose the reason for the key step. ### Find the mistake Read Ivy's working. Are both lengths in the same unit? ### Which lengths? ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a sail on the board, a shape with a missing corner (subtract), square metres to square centimetres, a two-step paint problem, then choosing a sensible unit." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#sail", height: 540 } tasks: - starter: "area.yml#sail" hint: "The sail's base is along the boom (3 m) and its height up the mast (5 m)." check: { type: board, text: "A sail is a right-angled triangle: 3 m along the bottom and 5 m up the mast. Make it and read its area.", when: "b = 3 and h = 5", explain: "½ × 3 × 5 = 7.5 m²." } - check: type: answer q: "A rectangular garden 8 m by 5 m has a 3 m by 2 m shed in one corner. What area of garden is left, in m²?" answer: "34" feedback: - ["46", "That adds the shed. Take it away."] - ["40", "That is the whole garden. Take away the shed."] explain: "8 × 5 − 3 × 2 = 40 − 6 = 34 m²." - check: type: answer q: "How many square centimetres are in 1 square metre?" answer: "10000" feedback: - ["100", "100 cm fit along each side, and 100 rows of them: 100 × 100."] explain: "1 m² is 100 cm by 100 cm: 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm²." - check: type: answer q: "A wall 5 m wide and 2.4 m high is painted. One litre of paint covers 4 m² (a made-up figure for this task). How many litres are needed?" answer: "3" feedback: - ["12", "12 m² is the area. Each litre covers 4 m²."] - ["48", "Divide the area by 4, not multiply."] explain: "5 × 2.4 = 12 m², and 12 ÷ 4 = 3 litres." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: which unit suits the area of a school oval?" options: ["m²", "cm²", "mm²", "m"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "cm² would give hundreds of millions: too small a unit.", "Far too small.", "m measures length, not area."] explain: "Square metres: an oval covers thousands of square metres (a 100 m by 100 m square is 10 000 m²)." ``` ### A sail Each task changes one thing. ### Take a part away ### Square units ### Two steps: paint ### A sensible unit ## Practise: area problems ```step stage: practise insight: "A split shape, a unit change and extra information, mixed; mixed units are the planted slip; the review keeps percentages fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A flag is a 10 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a triangle on one end: base 4 cm, height 3 cm. Total area, in cm²?" answer: "46" feedback: - ["52", "Halve the triangle: ½ × 4 × 3 = 6."] explain: "40 + 6 = 46 cm²." - check: type: answer q: "A path is 300 cm long and 2 m wide. Its area, in m²?" answer: "6" feedback: - ["600", "300 cm = 3 m. Then 3 × 2."] explain: "300 cm = 3 m, and 3 × 2 = 6 m²." - check: type: answer q: "A right-angled triangle has base 12 cm, height 5 cm and sloping side 13 cm. Area, in cm²?" answer: "30" feedback: - ["78", "13 is a slanted side. Use the height, 5 cm."] - ["60", "Halve it."] explain: "½ × 12 × 5 = 30 cm²." - check: type: answer q: "Review: find 25% of 48." answer: "12" feedback: - ["23", "That is 48 − 25. 25% is a quarter."] explain: "A quarter of 48: 12." ``` ### Split ### Convert ### Extra information ### Review: percentages ## Make: a tall sail ```step stage: make insight: "Designing a sail with a set area and a shape condition means searching base and height pairs, not just using a formula forwards." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#make", height: 540 } hint: ["½ × b × h = 12, so b × h = 24.", "Pick a pair where the height is bigger than the base."] check: { type: board, text: "Design a right-angled sail with area 12 m² that is taller than it is wide.", when: "a = 12 and h > b", explain: "b × h = 24 with h bigger: base 3 m and height 8 m, or base 4 m and height 6 m." } ``` Then work out the cost of the sailcloth at \$15 per m² (a made-up price for the task). ## Make: paint for a gable, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A gable is a triangle, and paint is bought by the litre: the area is one step, the coats a second (they cover the wall twice) and the tin's coverage a third." hint: ["Find the triangle's area first.", "Two coats cover the gable twice. How much area is that in all?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The triangular gable end of a house has a base of 8 m and a height of 3 m. One litre of paint covers 10 m², and the gable gets two coats. How many litres of paint are needed?" steps: - ["Gable: $\\tfrac{1}{2} \\times 8 \\times 3 = 12$ m²", "a triangle is half of base × height"] - ["Two coats: $12 \\times 2 = 24$ m² to cover", "each coat covers the whole gable again"] - ["Paint: $24 \\div 10 = 2.4$ litres", "each litre covers 10 m², so divide the area by 10"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is 24 m² the area to cover?" options: - "Two coats means covering the 12 m² twice" - "Two coats means covering half the area" - "Two coats means adding 2 m² to the area" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Two coats put on more paint, not less.", "The second coat covers the whole gable again, not just 2 m²."] answer: "2.4" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["1.2", "That is for one coat. Two coats cover the gable twice."] - ["24", "That is the area to cover. Each litre covers 10 m², so divide."] - ["12", "That is the area of the gable, not the litres."] criteria: - "I found the area of the triangle with half of base × height." - "I counted both coats before dividing by the coverage." - "My answer is in litres, not m²." explain: "½ × 8 × 3 = 12 m². Two coats: 24 m². At 10 m² per litre: 2.4 litres." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The gable, the coverage and the coats are made up for the task. A real job also takes the windows off, and rough walls drink more paint. Sketch the triangle, work it through, check it, and type the litres. **Also used in** - **Painting.** The coverage is printed on the tin, and a painter works out the area and the coats before buying. - **Sailmaking.** Cloth for a triangular sail is ordered by area, and the area also sets how much power the sail gives. - **Turf and lawn.** A wedge of lawn is a triangle: its area sets how much turf to buy. ```teacher summary: Students solve area problems by choosing the base and perpendicular height, converting to one unit, and splitting composite shapes into rectangles and triangles (adding or subtracting parts), with reasoning they own (AC9M7M01, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can pick the right base and height when a shape has extra lengths. - I can change lengths to the same unit before finding an area. - I can find the area of a shape made of rectangles and triangles. struggle: Planning a composite area before calculating. Ask students to sketch the parts and label each with its own lengths first; resist giving the split. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need the parallelogram and triangle formulas (previous lessons) and converting cm and m. The one idea: choose, convert, split. The common mistake is multiplying lengths in different units (Ivy's mistake); extra information (slanted sides) is planted in several tasks. 1 m² = 10 000 cm² surprises most students. The house-wall task is a reasoning check: the working is never marked, only the final area and the reason for the roof step. running: - "Predict: students who chose 1000 m² did not convert." - "Run: ask how the half-metre row shows on the grid." - "Investigate: ask two students to share different splits of the house wall." - "Modify: for 1 m², draw a 1 m square and ask how many 1 cm squares fit along one side." - "Make: compare designs, then cost them." - "Paper: the gable is worked in books; the page marks the litres and the reason picked for two coats (cover the area twice), then shows a model. Books out, and look for 24 m² written before the division." stuck: - see: A student multiplies cm by m (Ivy's mistake). ask: What unit is each length in? fix: Change both to metres (or both to cm) first. - see: A student uses every number given. ask: Which lengths meet at a right angle? fix: Use the base and its height; ignore slanted sides. - see: A student cannot start a composite shape. ask: Can you see a rectangle and a triangle in it? fix: Sketch the parts, find each area, then add (or subtract a missing part). stretch: Find the area of the letter L, T or H drawn on squared paper in two different ways (adding parts, and subtracting from a rectangle). support: Use squared paper; convert all lengths to the smaller unit and write them on the sketch. leads: > Next: Volume (AC9M7M02): the area of the base times the height. Where it leads: area of trapeziums, circles and composite shapes with circles (Year 8), and surface area (Year 9). exit: q: A shape is a 7 m by 4 m rectangle with a triangle on top (base 7 m, height 2 m). Find its area. a: 28 + ½ × 7 × 2 = 28 + 7 = 35 m². explain: > Area problems have three moves: - **Choose** the base and the height at a right angle to it; a slanted side is extra information. - **Convert** every length to the same unit first (250 cm = 2.5 m). Area is in square units, and 1 m² = 10 000 cm². - **Split** a shape into rectangles and triangles and add the parts, or subtract a missing part from a bigger shape. ```
